title: Two Surfaces, Not Twelve: Designing for Testability — Check

questions.prompt: Why does limiting the frontend to two surfaces (gateway + AI search) improve testability?
questions.explanation: With one gateway surface instead of twelve direct dependencies, a frontend test stubs a single contract, dramatically reducing brittleness and blast radius.
options: It makes the frontend faster at runtime
A frontend test must fake fewer HTTP surfaces, so it has fewer reasons to break
It removes the need for any backend tests
It guarantees the domain services never change

questions.prompt: In Agronomy Studio, the frontend calls each of the twelve domain microservices directly.
questions.explanation: The frontend talks to only two surfaces: the gateway (`/agronomy-api/*`) and the mock AI search. The gateway fans out to the domain services.

questions.prompt: Where do well-targeted tests in this architecture tend to live?
questions.explanation: Each boundary has observable inputs and outputs, so each layer can be asserted independently without standing up the rest of the system.
options: Only inside the Blazor UI components
At the system's defined boundaries: frontend↔gateway, gateway↔domain modules, domain↔upstreams
In a single end-to-end suite that exercises all twelve services at once
